changelog: v42d carries the SAME content as v42c -- it is a RE-RELEASE, not a change. The bench unit auto-applied v42c 4 minutes after the push, and GitHub's CDN served it the stale cached v42b packages/cytech.yaml (raw.githubusercontent.com caches each file for 5 minutes; no error, just old bytes), so the unit self-reports v42c while keeping the v42b package -- and can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date. v42d exists purely so devices re-fetch the package with a version comparison they will act on. (For consumers of v42c's changelog: v42c was about the Config Check row showing 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart -- the runtime integrity check now also runs right after every core start, so the row shows its real result (ok / restored / error) within minutes, and before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'.) Rest of the content below is unchanged from v42c. For the history: v42b fixed the row showing 'Entity not found' because Home Assistant pins an entity_id in its entity registry the first time a unique_id is seen -- renaming a sensor does not move a registered entity_id, so the sensor's unique_id was changed and every unit registers fresh as sensor.cytech_integrity_status (the id the row references); v42a was the earlier rename-only attempt that couldn't heal already-registered units. Units coming from v39 or older also get v42/v41/v40 below. v42 makes a corrupted configuration.yaml self-healing, and not just at boot: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check -- at boot and every 4 hours while running), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts (runtime corruption is repaired the same day it happens, before the next update's restart could land the system in HA recovery mode), and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are now also emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v42c also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
